name: Vermont
overview: Vermont has no county tax sales. Each town's or city's collector of delinquent taxes can levy on land with unpaid taxes and advertise it for sale at public auction in the town where it lies, with the last newspaper notice at least 10 days before the sale. The winning bidder buys the property subject to a right of redemption: the owner or mortgagee can redeem within one year from the day of sale by paying the collector who made the sale, with interest at one percent per month. If the property is not redeemed, the collector executes a deed to the purchaser.

counties.how_to_bid: Attend in person. The starting bid is the outstanding taxes plus all fees of the tax sale. Pay in certified funds (certified check, treasurer's check or money order); personal checks are not accepted, and any certified funds above the bid are refunded the day of the sale. The owner or lienholder has one year to redeem, and the bidder earns 1% interest per month on the bid until then. A buyer who gets the property pays current taxes, water and sewer charges, and transfer and recording fees at closing.
